banks.note: GENUINELY DIFFERENT from every other source: Axis's real retail rate table only exists in a downloadable PDF, not on any HTML page — the HTML landing page (deposits/fixed-deposits/fd-interest-rates) only shows 2 'popular' summary rows even after checking the dedicated FD-rates sub-page. fetch_and_track.py now has a PDF-specific fetch path (fetch_pdf_bytes) for content_type:'pdf' sources, and extract_axis_rows() (in extract_structured.py) uses pdfplumber's TABLE-aware extraction directly on the saved PDF file rather than flattening to text and regexing it. KNOWN CAVEAT: this PDF's URL is DATE-STAMPED ('...-14-august-26.pdf') — unlike every other bank's stable page URL, this exact URL will go stale (404, most likely) the next time Axis republishes rates under a new dated filename. When that happens this will surface as an honest fetch ERROR (not a silent wrong-data problem), and the URL will need re-discovering from the landing page's 'VIEW RATES' link by hand — auto-discovering the current PDF link was explicitly out of scope for this pass. IMPORTANT: `content_type: 'pdf'` above applies ONLY to the fd_rates URL — home_loan is a normal HTML page; fetch_and_track.py's per-URL-type loop deliberately does NOT apply this bank-level flag to any URL type except fd_rates, specifically to avoid this exact bank breaking its own new home_loan fetch.

banks.note: CONFIRMED (2026-08-15): this page never reaches Playwright's default 'networkidle' wait condition — some persistent background request (analytics/chat widget, never identified further, not worth chasing) keeps the network from settling, so the default wait_until times out every time even though the real rate table itself renders almost immediately. fetch_source() now supports a per-source 'wait_until' override (this config field) plus a fixed 3s settle wait after goto() whenever a non-default wait_until is used, since a weaker wait condition doesn't guarantee the DOM has actually finished rendering the instant goto() returns. 'commit' (page has started receiving a response) was confirmed to reliably load this page's real content.
